text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Wednesday:

- High Court in the canton of Appenzell-Ausserrhoden confirmed its previous verdict against Ernst Reimers, a head of the Universal Church, who it found guilty of racial discrimination. Reimers was imprisoned for four months and fined 5,000 Swiss francs for having sent out hundreds of letters to sect members that contained crass anti-semitic remarks.
- The International Federation of the Red Cross has started a lottery on the Internet in an attempt to raise funds. The first numbers will be drawn on April 18 in Liechtenstein.
- Investments in industry and building in Switzerland will decline this year, according to a survey by the Federal Institute of Technology.
- Pharmaceuticals group Novartis increased its net profit (excluding extraordinary costs) by two percent to 4.2 billion Swiss francs in 1996.
- Berne-based pharmaceuticals firm Galenica announced it will cut 168 jobs in the next two and a half years.
- Maverick banker Martin Ebner is launching a nationwide campaign to promote investing in stocks in efforts to win more customers in Switzerland.
- The Swiss military is looking for ways to find more officers as fewer and fewer people in management positions are willing to take on two careers.
- Conglomerate Daetwyler's 1996 profit rose by 6.3 percent to 21.3 million Swiss francs.

- Sulzer AG's chief executive Fritz Fahrni was disappointed with group 1996 results despite a net profit of 82 million Swiss francs, down from 92 million in 1995. Sulzer is optimistic about this year and expects a considerable increase in profit.
- Laiteries Reunies de Geneve posted sales of 223.3 million Swiss francs in 1996, a decrease of 3.5 percent compared to 1995.
